candidates.decision_summary: Task1 targets the same observational focal claim: under SMD rules, plurality vote winners should be closer to the median voter than under PR, using the Manifesto-method pldist1 outcome. The original paper describes cross-national country-election data and Manifesto, citizen-expert, and citizen-perception approaches; the focal H4a-type claim concerns the distance from the median voter to the plurality vote winner under SMD. The authorized dataset was verified as 331 country-election rows, 107 columns, with pldist1 continuous and nonmissing, smd coded pr/smd/missing, year 1945-2003, and repeated country observations across 20 countries. The candidate uses the authorized Stata file, pldist1 in raw units, a binary SMD-minus-PR contrast, excludes only missing/non-focal election-rule observations and missing country needed for the declared fixed effects, and reports sample flow. The code reads value-labeled Stata data with convert_categoricals=True, constructs smd_clean and smd_bin, performs within-country demeaning, estimates OLS without an intercept using country-clustered standard errors, and writes/prints the focal coefficient, uncertainty, sample counts, and conclusion. The country fixed effect is an explicit, justified model deviation for repeated country-election observations and does not change the focal outcome, contrast, or dataset. This is distinct from shared-memory paths using decade-adjusted OLS, simple OLS, quantile regression, Gamma GLM, Mann-Whitney/Hodges-Lehmann, log-outcome OLS, and permutation tests. No low-quality rule is triggered under M1-M6 or Task1 rules 1.1-1.9; guardrails G1, G8, and G14 apply because a different defensible model/SE choice from the original or from evaluator preference is not by itself a defect.

The candidate satisfies those requirements by using the authorized Powell Stata file, applying the 1945-2003 inclusive year restriction, using pldist1 as the Manifesto-method plurality-winner distance outcome, and comparing SMD versus PR through smd_bin. The original paper summary confirms the paper's observational cross-national election design, Manifesto-method analyses over the postwar period through 2003, and the theoretical claim that SMD party competition should place the plurality winner near the median voter. Dataset inspection verified 331 country-election observations, year range 1945-2003 with no missing years, pldist1 nonmissing and continuous, smd labels pr/smd/missing, and repeated observations within countries. The candidate's country fixed-effects model is an explicit, methodologically justified robustness deviation for repeated country-election observations and still produces a comparable SMD-minus-PR coefficient on the required Manifesto outcome in the required time window. The Task2 code matches the plan: it reads the authorized dataset with categorical labels, applies the year restriction, documents all material exclusions, constructs smd_bin, demeans within country, estimates the no-intercept within OLS with country-clustered standard errors, and reports the focal coefficient, p-value, confidence interval, sample counts, and conclusion. No Task2 instruction-compliance defect is present, and no low-quality rule is triggered under M1-M6 or Task2 rules 2.1-2.8. Guardrails G1, G4, G8, and G14 apply because the use of a defensible adjusted model or reuse of a Task1-like implementation is not low-quality when all Task2 requirements are met.
